:::: {#hero-heading}
::: h1
Welcome
:::

I am glad you are here!

I am a Bioinformatics Scientist at the [University of Vermont](https://www.uvm.edu/), Department of Microbiology and Molecular Genetics. My research focuses on collaborative bioinformatics and computational biology, spanning variant analysis, epigenomics, virus typing, transcriptomics, and structural biology. I work extensively with workflow management systems, containerized environments, and high-performance computing to enforce reproducibility and scalability.

I have been integrating quantitative sciences and computational methods with biomedical research since 2001, with a focus on Bayesian statistical methods, machine learning, data science and now, increasingly, AI-augmented methods". Learn more about my work in [projects](/projects) and  [publications](/publication).

Get in touch by [sending me a note](/contact.qmd)! {{< fa feather-pointed >}}

**A bit longer...**

I grew up in Costa Rica in a family of life scientists, and by the way, when I was a teenager I swore never to have anything to do with biology or get a Ph.D -- my aspirations leaned more towards becoming a ninja...but alas...decades later with a PhD in bioinformatics!

During my first semester of [Computer Science](https://www.ecci.ucr.ac.cr/) at the University of Costa Rica I had a classmate/friend that was studying pure mathematics. Something about the way he thought and his approach to solving problems really intrigued me. I took a class and the fascinating world of math proved to be a welcome challenge so I decided to also [study math](https://emate.ucr.ac.cr/) (my family was also much more supportive of that than of me becoming a ninja!). I had no idea that studying math would later open a world of possibilities.

After graduating I took a break from school and came to Vermont to live at a [Zen Buddhist Center](https://vermontzen.org/), where I also had my very first and very cold Vermont winter! Eventually I met Dr. Jeff Bond, a University of Vermont researcher and professor, whom I worked with for 5 years as a bioinformatics programmer and afterwards he was my advisor for the Ph.D. program in [Cell and Molecular Biology](https://www.uvm.edu/graduate/cmb) doing Computational Biology/Bioinformatics.

During my second year of the Ph.D program, something unexpected happen: another graduate student and myself took a visiting professor (Terry Speed, a world-renowned bioinformatics statistician) to Vermont's famous ice cream factory: Ben and Jerry's. During the trip, something about the conversation, and also listening to his talks, really aroused my interest in statistics, subsequently I took a Bayesian statistics course and I was hooked! Been a statistician/bioinformatician/data scientist ever since working for both academia and industry. 

I also have a life outside of work, mainly about finding the [meaning of life and becoming a better person](https://vermontzen.org), and also as a hobby singing and playing percussion in a [band](https://songoros.com/), but that's a story for another time!!
::::
